The skill's clearest value is on opinionated-pushback scenarios: evals 1 (whole life, +40pp), 2 (dividends, +40pp), 3 (market timing, +40pp), 4 (waterfall, +60pp), 9 (lump sum, +40pp). These are exactly the cases where generic advice gives wrong answers.

Eval 4 (investment waterfall) is the most discriminating eval: without_skill scored only 20% (1/5) because baseline Claude incorrectly prioritized HSA contributions before paying off 24% credit card debt — inverting the canonical waterfall. The skill enforced the correct order.

Eval 4 with_skill scored 80% (4/5), not 100%: the skill's response recommended an optional $50-100/month HSA split alongside debt paydown, which was flagged as violating the strict all-in-on-debt position. This is a real edge case worth addressing in the skill.

Eval 3 (market timing) without_skill got 60% — the grader failed assertion 3 because the baseline cited Schwab's lump-sum research rather than Vanguard's. This assertion may be too brand-specific; consider loosening it to accept any credible research citation.

Eval 9 (windfall/DCA) without_skill got 60% — baseline Claude cited Vanguard correctly (assertion 1 passed) but recommended 6-12 months DCA instead of 3-6 months (assertion 4 failed) and didn't explicitly frame 3-year DCA as market timing (assertion 5 failed). Eval 7 (AUM advisor) without_skill scored 80% — the only miss was not mentioning bogleheads.org. This is a minor but meaningful differentiator: the skill consistently points to community resources.
